core.title: Declare exactly one primary artifact as a train's terminal contract
core.given: A train exists or is being defined, wherever its definition is stored.
core.when: The train's terminal step artifact or its family is defined, changed, or checked (either one alone is enough).
core.then: The train's terminal step declares exactly one primary artifact, which is the train's terminal contract.
prefer: Name one primary artifact on the final step and treat it as the terminal contract: the source of truth for the train's family.

Derive the family from the terminal contract: set family = delivery only if the terminal contract BOTH requires an Acceptance Authority commit AND terminates in platform:acceptance:commit-receipt; in every other case set family = behavior.
Whenever either the terminal artifact or the family changes alone, re-apply the derivation above and make the declared family match its result.
avoid: Declaring zero or several primary artifacts on the terminal step.
Deriving, guessing or asserting the family from the train id (or its name/prefix) — never do this; only the terminal contract decides.
Declaring delivery when only one of the two delivery conditions holds.
core.why: One declared terminal contract is the single unambiguous source of truth for what a train delivers, so its family is derived from it and never from the train id.
evidence: The train's terminal step lists exactly one primary artifact.

Family is consistent with the terminal contract: delivery iff the contract requires an Acceptance Authority commit and terminates in platform:acceptance:commit-receipt; otherwise behavior — regardless of what the train id suggests.
verification: Scope: the check covers every train definition, irrespective of file path or author role; the train-definition location patterns supplied by the profile are discovery hints only — a train stored outside them is still in scope.

The check verifies that a train's terminal step lists exactly one primary artifact, and that the declared family equals the family derived from that contract: delivery iff the contract both requires an Acceptance Authority commit and terminates in platform:acceptance:commit-receipt; anything else maps to behavior; both delivery conditions are required, and a family merely asserted from the train id does not satisfy the check.
Glossary used by the check: the terminal contract is the declared primary artifact of a train's final step; the train's family (behavior|delivery) is derived from it, never from the train id.

values: train terminal step or its artifact added/modified
train checked for terminal contract or family

fires: A new train is defined, including its final step.
The artifacts of an existing train's terminal step are changed, even if the family is untouched.
A train's family (behavior|delivery) is set or changed, even if the terminal step is untouched.
A train definition is reviewed or checked for its terminal contract or family.
doesNotFire: Only intermediate (non-terminal) steps of a train are edited and neither the terminal step nor the family is defined, changed or checked.
Work on wagons, WMBTs, acceptances or docs that does not define, change or check any train.

profileRequirements.meaning: Discovery patterns for train-definition files (a plan-artifact kind), used only as non-exhaustive activation hints: the obligation holds for every train definition wherever it is stored, and a train outside these patterns is still in scope.

neutralityNotes: This convention is method-level rather than stack-mechanical: trains, terminal steps, primary artifacts, family (behavior|delivery), the Acceptance Authority and the platform acceptance commit-receipt terminal step are ATDD methodology concepts that appear verbatim in the canonical source, so the core carries them unchanged and bunOnly is empty. The only concrete, layout-specific content is the train-definition discovery path globs (including a file suffix), which the core cannot name; they moved to the profile under roles.plan_artifact.path and remain non-exhaustive discovery hints — verification keeps the Bun text's deference that a train outside the patterns is still in scope. The Bun sidecar's path_glob activation fact type has no neutral counterpart in the core fact vocabulary, so it is re-expressed as a file_kind fact ('train definition') whose concrete recognition patterns come from the profile. bun.json declares no severity or disposition, so core.verification states none.
